## Experience

- URL: https://idigdata.com/experience/
- Title: Experience | idigdata
- Description: 20+ years of business leadership, over 50 enterprise transformations, and three years of hands-on agentic development across Data Integration Group, Sierra Nevada Brewing Co., Access IT, and Timberline Architectural Openings.
- Career Arc:
  1. Founder & Principal — Data Integration Group (DIG LLC) (2016–Present): Enterprise transformation, ERP recovery ($10M program recovered and delivered for $8M), post-acquisition integration ($350M business close reduced from 18 days to 4 days), and multi-facility IBP/S&OP ($200M wine producer).
  2. Chief Information Officer (Embedded Executive Mandate via DIG) — Sierra Nevada Brewing Co. (2024–2026): $15M CIO mandate, executive leadership team & board reporting, 26 months of architecture and implementation across 25 task forces and 150 participants, IS/IT rebuild, company-owned data core, and production agentic workflows.
  3. Lead Consultant & Solution Architect — Access IT, Inc. (2012–2016): Partner-side Microsoft Dynamics NAV and ContractERP delivery across manufacturing, construction, distribution, and services.
  4. Founder, CEO & CTO — Timberline Architectural Openings (1996–2012): Built and scaled a contractor, manufacturer, and distributor from $250K in year one to $130M by year ten with 100+ employees across Las Vegas and Macau projects; built proprietary enterprise software.

## Agentic AI

- URL: https://idigdata.com/agentic-ai/
- Title: Learn through the work · Dispatches from the Operational Seam | Robert Paddock
- Description: Field notes on enterprise transformation, operating knowledge, and hands-on agentic software development by Robert Paddock.
- Core Themes:
  - Binary Intelligence & One Man and a Context Window: Human judgment directing binary intelligence (zeros and ones), equalizing capability from the CEO's desk to the shop floor.
  - Chapter One (The Business as It Actually Runs): Reconciling Finance's formal close with Operations' live shop-floor reality through Integrated Business Planning (IBP), evolved from S&OP, with frontline operators as co-architects.
  - Chapter Two (Working with Intelligence): Separating running, proposing, and authorizing a workflow; deterministic rules before agentic inference; auditability and human sign-off on consequential actions.
  - Chapter Three (The Machine That Builds the Machines That Build the Workflows): Multi-vendor, multi-harness engineering with independent opposing-model verification to catch physical/financial edge cases (such as split-pallet partial receipts and catch-weight variances) before production cutover.
- Field Dispatches:
  - https://idigdata.com/agentic-ai/marys-sheet/ — Mary's Sheet: Operational reality vs. green ERP screens and Integrated Business Planning (IBP).
  - https://idigdata.com/agentic-ai/the-delivery-seam/ — The Delivery Seam: Separating running, proposing, and authorizing an enterprise workflow.
  - https://idigdata.com/agentic-ai/the-application-layer/ — The Application Layer: Multi-harness verification and catching physical cutover traps.
- Feed: https://idigdata.com/feed.xml (RSS 2.0, "Agentic AI, by Robert Paddock")

## The Collective

- URL: https://idigdata.com/collective/
- Title: The Collective · Three Systems, One Set of Patterns | Robert Paddock
- Description: How B.O.S.S. (Living Digital Twin), FlowCraft (The Live Operating Instance), and The Rig (The Machine That Builds the Machines) run on a shared spine (org -> instance -> assets -> outcomes) and loop (intent, define, build, outcome).
- The Three Systems:
  1. B.O.S.S. (Where the Business Stands — The Front End of Everything · Living Digital Twin): Maps where the business actually stands, organizes the data core, builds a living digital twin across 6 process constellations (P2P, O2C, P2M, S2S, D2R, MDM), runs project and change management, builds workflows from where the company stands, and monitors the live operating instance.
  2. FlowCraft (The Business as It Runs — The Live Operating Instance): The operating instance of an operating company (DigOps) where real daily transactions run—Purchase Orders, Payroll, Receiving & Floor Dock, Approvals, and Close & Reconciliation—built from B.O.S.S. and monitored by B.O.S.S.
  3. The Rig (The Foundry — The Machine That Builds the Machines): Multi-vendor, multi-harness engineering foundry with shared comms, durable memory that outlasts the session, and independent opposing-model check gates before anything lands.
